import csv
import io
import os
import shutil
import tempfile

import requests

GHCN_URL = (
    "https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/global-historical-climatology-network-daily/"
    "access/USC00351862.csv"
)


def _curate_copy(src, dst):
    """Copy a file unless src and dst are the same path (added by migrate_catalog.py)."""
    if os.path.abspath(src) != os.path.abspath(dst):
        shutil.copyfile(src, dst)


def main(inputs, outputs, params):
    """Download the NOAA GHCN-Daily CSV for station USC00351862 and upload it unchanged."""
    output1 = outputs["output1"]
    print(f"Downloading GHCN-Daily station CSV from {GHCN_URL}", flush=True)
    try:
        resp = requests.get(GHCN_URL, timeout=300)
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: failed to download {GHCN_URL}: {e}", flush=True)
        raise

    content = resp.content
    if not content or not content.strip():
        msg = f"ERROR: empty response from {GHCN_URL}"
        print(msg, flush=True)
        raise RuntimeError(msg)

    # Validate header contains a DATE column
    first_line = content.split(b"\n", 1)[0].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    header = next(csv.reader(io.StringIO(first_line)), [])
    header = [h.strip().strip('"') for h in header]
    if "DATE" not in header:
        msg = f"ERROR: downloaded CSV has no DATE column; header: {header[:20]}"
        print(msg, flush=True)
        raise RuntimeError(msg)

    n_lines = content.count(b"\n")
    print(f"Downloaded {len(content)} bytes, ~{n_lines} lines; columns: {len(header)}", flush=True)

    tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    local_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "USC00351862_daily.csv")
    with open(local_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(content)

    _curate_copy(local_path, output1)
    print(f"Uploaded station CSV to ./{output1}", flush=True)

nodes.name: process_weather_variable
nodes.description: Runs in parallel, one instance per variable: precipitation (PRCP), minimum temperature (TMIN) and maximum temperature (TMAX), selected by rank (rank 1 = PRCP, rank 2 = TMIN, rank 3 = TMAX, via faasr_rank()). Reads the downloaded station CSV. For its variable: take the values from 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-01, and the daily average over the same dates in each of the previous 10 years (extend that window by 30 days). Temperatures in the data are in tenths of a degree Celsius. Exact interpretation (user-confirmed): this year's values cover 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-01 only. The 10-year baseline uses 2015-2024, and ONLY the baseline window is extended, by 30 days after the end date: Jan 1 to Mar 31 of each baseline year. For each calendar month-day in Jan 1..Mar 31, average the variable across the 10 baseline years (ignoring missing values; Feb 29 averages only the leap years present). Units: keep PRCP exactly as reported in the CSV, with no unit conversion; only convert TMIN and TMAX from tenths of degrees Celsius to degrees Celsius (divide by 10). Write one ranked output per instance: a CSV with columns date (2025 calendar date for the month-day, Jan 1..Mar 31; Feb 29 dropped since 2025 has none), variable, this_year (empty after 2025-03-01 or where missing), ten_year_avg.

outputs.description: Per-variable daily series (rank 1=PRCP, 2=TMIN, 3=TMAX), Jan 1-Mar 31: date, variable, this_year (to Mar 1), ten_year_avg

import os
import shutil
import tempfile

import pandas as pd

RANK_VARIABLES = {1: "PRCP", 2: "TMIN", 3: "TMAX"}
THIS_YEAR = 2025
THIS_START = pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01")
THIS_END = pd.Timestamp("2025-03-01")
BASELINE_YEARS = list(range(2015, 2025))  # previous 10 years: 2015..2024
# Baseline window extended by 30 days after Mar 1 -> Jan 1 .. Mar 31 of each year
BASELINE_END_MONTH_DAY = (3, 31)


def _curate_copy(src, dst):
    """Copy a file unless src and dst are the same path (added by migrate_catalog.py)."""
    if os.path.abspath(src) != os.path.abspath(dst):
        shutil.copyfile(src, dst)


def main(inputs, outputs, params):
    input1 = inputs["input1"]
    output1 = outputs["output1"]
    r = {"rank": params["rank"], "max_rank": params["max_rank"]}
    rank = int(r["rank"])
    if rank not in RANK_VARIABLES:
        msg = f"ERROR: unexpected rank {rank}; expected 1..3"
        print(msg, flush=True)
        raise ValueError(msg)
    var = RANK_VARIABLES[rank]
    in_name = input1 if "{rank}" in input1 else input1
    out_name = output1
    print(f"Rank {rank}: processing {var} from ./{in_name}", flush=True)

    tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    local_in = os.path.join(tmpdir, "station.csv")
    _curate_copy(in_name, local_in)

    df = pd.read_csv(local_in, usecols=lambda c: c in ("DATE", var), dtype=str)
    if "DATE" not in df.columns or var not in df.columns:
        msg = f"ERROR: input CSV missing DATE or {var} column"
        print(msg, flush=True)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    df["DATE"] = pd.to_datetime(df["DATE"].str.strip(), errors="coerce")
    df[var] = pd.to_numeric(df[var].str.strip(), errors="coerce")
    df = df.dropna(subset=["DATE"])
    if var in ("TMIN", "TMAX"):
        # tenths of degrees Celsius -> degrees Celsius
        df[var] = df[var] / 10.0
    # PRCP is kept exactly as reported (no unit conversion)

    df["month"] = df["DATE"].dt.month
    df["day"] = df["DATE"].dt.day
    in_window = (df["month"] <= 2) | (
        (df["month"] == 3) & (df["day"] <= BASELINE_END_MONTH_DAY[1])
    )

    base = df[df["DATE"].dt.year.isin(BASELINE_YEARS) & in_window]
    base = base.dropna(subset=[var])
    if base.empty:
        msg = f"ERROR: no {var} data for baseline years {BASELINE_YEARS[0]}-{BASELINE_YEARS[-1]}"
        print(msg, flush=True)
        raise ValueError(msg)
    avg = base.groupby(["month", "day"])[var].mean()

    this = df[(df["DATE"] >= THIS_START) & (df["DATE"] <= THIS_END)].set_index("DATE")[var]
    if this.dropna().empty:
        msg = f"ERROR: no {var} data between {THIS_START.date()} and {THIS_END.date()}"
        print(msg, flush=True)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    dates = pd.date_range(f"{THIS_YEAR}-01-01", f"{THIS_YEAR}-03-31", freq="D")
    rows = []
    for d in dates:
        ty = this.get(d) if d <= THIS_END else None
        ty = None if ty is None or pd.isna(ty) else float(ty)
        ta = avg.get((d.month, d.day))
        ta = None if ta is None or pd.isna(ta) else float(ta)
        rows.append(
            {
                "date": d.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
                "variable": var,
                "this_year": ty,
                "ten_year_avg": ta,
            }
        )
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["date", "variable", "this_year", "ten_year_avg"])

    local_out = os.path.join(tmpdir, out_name)
    out.to_csv(local_out, index=False)
    _curate_copy(local_out, out_name)
    print(f"Rank {rank}: wrote {len(out)} rows for {var} "
        f"({out['this_year'].notna().sum()} this-year values) to ./{out_name}", flush=True)

nodes.name: plot_weather_comparison
nodes.description: Runs once after all three parallel variable-processing instances finish. Reads the three per-variable result CSVs (one per rank: 1 = PRCP, 2 = TMIN, 3 = TMAX). Plot a figure with three panels (precipitation, max temperature, min temperature) showing this year as a solid line and the 10-year average as a dashed line. The plot covers 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-01 only (drop rows after 2025-03-01 even though the inputs' baseline extends to Mar 31). Panels are stacked vertically sharing the date x-axis; precipitation is plotted as reported in the CSV with no unit conversion (y-label: 'Precipitation (as reported, tenths of mm)'), temperatures in degrees Celsius. Include a legend and a title naming Corvallis, OR (USC00351862), winter 2025 vs 2015-2024 average. Use a headless matplotlib backend (Agg) and upload the figure as a PNG to the S3 data store.

import os

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.dates as mdates  # noqa: E402
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402

PLOT_START = pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01")
PLOT_END = pd.Timestamp("2025-03-01")

# Panel order: precipitation, max temperature, min temperature
PANELS = [
    ("PRCP", "Precipitation", "Precipitation (as reported, tenths of mm)"),
    ("TMAX", "Maximum temperature", "Max temperature (°C)"),
    ("TMIN", "Minimum temperature", "Min temperature (°C)"),
]


def main(inputs, outputs, params):
    # inputs["input1"] is a folder holding every per-variable comparison file
    # (winter_comparison_<rank>.csv), and only those.
    folder = inputs["input1"]
    names = sorted(os.listdir(folder))
    if not names:
        msg = f"ERROR: the input folder {folder} holds no comparison files"
        print(msg, flush=True)
        raise FileNotFoundError(msg)
    print(f"Found {len(names)} comparison files: {names}", flush=True)

    frames = []
    for name in names:
        df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(folder, name))
        required = {"date", "variable", "this_year", "ten_year_avg"}
        if not required.issubset(df.columns):
            msg = f"ERROR: {name} missing columns {sorted(required - set(df.columns))}"
            print(msg, flush=True)
            raise ValueError(msg)
        frames.append(df)

    data = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    data["date"] = pd.to_datetime(data["date"], errors="coerce")
    data["this_year"] = pd.to_numeric(data["this_year"], errors="coerce")
    data["ten_year_avg"] = pd.to_numeric(data["ten_year_avg"], errors="coerce")
    data = data.dropna(subset=["date"])
    data = data[(data["date"] >= PLOT_START) & (data["date"] <= PLOT_END)]

    missing = [v for v, _, _ in PANELS if v not in set(data["variable"])]
    if missing:
        msg = f"ERROR: no data for variable(s) {missing} in inputs"
        print(msg, flush=True)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(PANELS), 1, figsize=(11, 10), sharex=True)
    for ax, (var, title, ylabel) in zip(axes, PANELS):
        sub = data[data["variable"] == var].sort_values("date")
        ax.plot(sub["date"], sub["this_year"], linestyle="-", color="tab:blue",
                label="Winter 2025")
        ax.plot(sub["date"], sub["ten_year_avg"], linestyle="--", color="tab:orange",
                label="2015-2024 average")
        ax.set_title(title)
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        ax.legend(loc="upper right")
    axes[-1].set_xlabel("Date")
    axes[-1].set_xlim(PLOT_START, PLOT_END)
    axes[-1].xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b %d"))
    fig.suptitle("Corvallis, OR (USC00351862): winter 2025 vs 2015-2024 average")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.97))

    fig.savefig(outputs["output1"], dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f"Wrote figure to {outputs['output1']}", flush=True)
